$comment: RC2 §11 (consumer retry rules) and §17 (retryable flags). auto_retry_permitted is copied directly from the error table's retryable column — it is not a separate business decision, it IS that column, restated here as an explicit consumer-facing policy fixture per §22.1's request for 'consumer and reverse-proxy vectors proving that answer_validation_failed is not automatically retried despite its 503 status.'
rule: The consumer may make at most one automatic retry, with the same canonical request and Idempotency-Key, using a fresh JWT and X-Request-ID, only for a transport failure or a response whose code has auto_retry_permitted=true below. Validation, authentication, authorization, version, invalidation, and idempotency-conflict codes are never auto-retried, regardless of HTTP status.

codes.note: The load-bearing case: HTTP 503 normally reads as retryable to generic tooling. RC2 §17 and acceptance criterion 33 are explicit that this specific code must never be auto-retried despite that status. A conformant reverse proxy or HTTP client library configured to blanket-retry 5xx responses is NOT conformant unless it special-cases this code.
